title: Pair Engram's carried-failure rule (w-004927a1fe2a): parse acceptance_evaluation.carried_failure and evaluation.revised_by/supersedes, brief the evaluator on the retired failed verdict and the criteria before/after, and pass --supersedes RECORD_ID host-side
outcome: Pair Engram's carried-failure rule (w-004927a1fe2a): parse acceptance_evaluation.carried_failure and evaluation.revised_by/supersedes, brief the evaluator on the retired failed verdict and the criteria before/after, and pass --supersedes RECORD_ID host-side
acceptance: Engram's refusals carried_failure_unacknowledged, carried_failure_self_acknowledged and nothing_to_supersede reach the requester with Engram's remedy text unchanged; a test shows it.
TermAl's feature documentation of acceptance evaluation describes the carried failure, who may name it, and what the evaluator is shown, and links Engram's R11.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

The host reads acceptance_evaluation.carried_failure from show --json (evaluation, revised_by, judged_revision, failing, supersedes_required) and work.evaluation.carried_failure from show --full (judged_criteria, blocking, judged_bindings, newest_judged_bindings) leniently: with the fields absent, as from an Engram older than e450eb0, a request behaves as it does today; a test shows both.

When a failure is carried, the evaluator's brief states the original failure's non-passing verdicts with their rationale, and the criteria and bindings it judged, those of a later failing evaluation that named it when there is one, and the current ones; a test shows the brief with and without the middle contract.
When a failure is carried, the evaluator's submission passes the carried record's id as supersedes; for an item with no carried failure it passes none; a test shows both.
When supersedes_required is true the host never selects same_session, nor a sub_agent under a session that holds, held or executes the run, and the request's answer says why; a test shows it.
